plan: With 3 bidders and uniform values on [0,49], the symmetric Nash equilibrium bidding strategy in a first-price auction is to bid (n-1)/n of your value, which equals 2/3 for n=3. This balances the trade-off between winning probability and profit margin. My value is $39, so I'll bid approximately 2/3 × 39 = $26. This maximizes expected profit given optimal competitor behavior.

With 3 bidders and uniform values on [0,49], the standard first-price auction equilibrium bid shading factor is (n-1)/n = 2/3. My value is $34, so optimal bid ≈ 34 × (2/3) ≈ 22.7. This balances winning probability against profit margin, avoiding overpaying while still competitive against other rational bidders using similar strategies.

With 3 bidders and uniform values on [0,49], the symmetric Bayesian-Nash equilibrium bid for a first-price auction is b(v) = v*(n-1)/n = v*2/3. This balances winning probability against profit margin. For v=45, optimal bid ≈ 30. I'll bid 30 to maximize expected profit while maintaining a reasonable chance of winning against the other two bidders' potentially high values.
